extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners working on satire/irony/sarcasm detection, dataset creators, and ML engineers evaluating language models
extracted.subtask_description: Creation and evaluation of a sentence-level dataset for satire detection (Romanian) and baseline experimental protocols for training and evaluating models in zero-shot and fine-tuning settings. Includes annotation, preprocessing, dataset splits, baseline models, and evaluation/reporting guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level annotation labels and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotators were instructed to label sentences as satirical, neutral, or uncertain. Samples with uncertain labels were discarded. The final dataset comprises sentences annotated by at least three annotators; the final label is determined by majority voting (the label common to at least two annotators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple native speakers; track annotator demographics (authors report six native Romanian-speaking students, ages 20–25, two male and four female). Ensure each sentence has annotations from ≥3 annotators; discard uncertain labels before forming majority vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-annotator agreement measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and report inter-annotator agreement using multiple metrics: Fleiss' Kappa, Kendall’s W, average Cohen’s Kappa, percentage agreement, and human-level performance (agreement of individual annotators with majority vote).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report values (paper reports Fleiss’ Kappa=0.4036, Kendall’s W=0.4378, avg Cohen’s Kappa=0.4053, avg percent agreement=71.1%, human-level performance=85.5%) to contextualize annotation difficulty and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and manual filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect data from satirical and non-satirical news outlets (paper cut-off date: February 2018) and perform manual filtering to remove articles containing inappropriate language, celebrity names, or references to sensitive or potentially controversial topics (including those related to religious institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use web scraping (authors used Scrapy), extract article titles and contents, apply manual inspection to remove problematic items early (authors reduced 10,806 titles to 3,692 after filtering). Document cut-off date and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization of named entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymize texts by identifying and removing named entities using a NER tool (authors used Spacy) and replacing occurrences with tags such as <PERSON>, <NORP>, <GPE>, <ORG>, <LOC>, and <FAC>. Also filter out URLs with an @URL tag and manually filter entities missed by the NER model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve placeholder tags during later preprocessing. Anonymization aims to reduce potential unwanted biases related to personalities and institutions and to address ethical concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-processing to reduce satirical-cue leakage
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a pre-processed variant where anonymized text is lowercased, incorrect diacritics are corrected (e.g., replace cedilla forms), tokenized with Spacy, stop words, punctuation, and short tokens (≤3 characters) are removed, and tokens are lemmatized. Placeholder tags remain unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the pre-processed version for classical ML methods (e.g., SVMs) and text analysis; document each step to allow reproducibility and to reduce leakage of stylistic or structural satirical cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide multiple dataset variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Release at least two dataset variants: an anonymized version and an anonymized + pre-processed version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make both variants publicly available to support different use cases (modern neural fine-tuning vs. classical ML/text analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping sentences by article in data splits
rubrics_metrics.description: When splitting into train/validation/test, group sentences from the same news article into the same split to avoid leaking contextual information across splits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors propose splits with train=9,800, validation≈2,000, test≈2,000 samples; enforce article-level grouping to prevent contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report dataset statistics and topic distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide dataset statistics such as counts per label, token counts per split, sentence length distributions (word/character means, medians, quartiles), domain distributions, and topic distributions (authors used BERTopic to identify topics with a minimum topic size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tables/figures for domain/topic coverage, token counts, and length statistics to help interpret model performance and dataset biases (authors report 8,179 regular and 5,694 satirical sentences, total 13,873).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics and reporting protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate models using accuracy and F1-score computed on the test set; run experiments multiple times and report mean and standard deviation; perform statistical significance testing (authors run experiments 5 times and use Student’s t-test, reporting p<0.01 for significance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run repeated trials (≥5) to estimate variance; report mean ± std; note significance tests and p-values when comparing models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline model selection and comparison settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate a diverse set of baselines including pretrained language models (Romanian BERT, RoGPT2), open-source LLM families (Gemma 3 at multiple sizes, RoMistral, RoLlama, RoGemma, Llama 3.1), and closed-source models (GPT-4o family, GPT-4.1, o4-mini), in both zero-shot and fine-tuning settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Romanian-specific models and multiple model sizes; compare zero-shot vs fine-tuning performance and report both to show gaps and strengths across settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental reproducibility: hyperparameters and training details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed training and fine-tuning hyperparameters: optimizer type (Adam/AdamW), learning rates, weight decay, number of epochs, batch sizes, frozen vs unfrozen layers, QLoRA 4-bit quantization and LoRA settings (R=16, α=32, dropout=0.05), scheduler/warmup, max input length, and hardware used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors give concrete settings (e.g., BERT: Adam weight decay 0.01, lr=2e-3, 40 epochs, batch 64; LLM fine-tuning: QLoRA, lr up to 1e-4, 3 epochs, batch 32, max input length 1024). Document inference hardware (authors used NVIDIA H100 80GB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inference prompting and parameter control
rubrics_metrics.description: For inference-only (zero-shot) models, provide a prompt specifying output format and insert classes in random order to avoid position bias. Use specified decoding settings (authors: default temperature 0.8, top-k=64, top-p=0.95, max output tokens=50; exceptions listed per model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate prompt complexity for fine-tuned models (shorter prompts) vs inference-only; randomize class order; document temperature/top-k/top-p/max tokens per model for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Address copyright and ethical issues: retain original copyright with authors, release dataset for academic purposes under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, anonymize entities to minimize bias and discrimination, and filter out harmful content via manual and automatic inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the license, anonymization steps, filtering policies, and the intent (do not endorse original article views). Keep records of manual inspections and filtering criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model behavior analysis and error type reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze and report model error types and per-topic performance: note tendencies such as higher false positive rates (Type I errors) in zero-shot settings and reduction of FPR after fine-tuning; report FNRs and topic-specific F1 variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide confusion analysis and per-topic/per-domain breakdowns (authors report Gemma 3 FPR 32–52% in zero-shot, reduced to <20% after fine-tuning; FNR <15%; topic-specific F1 differences). Use these insights to guide future improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report human-level performance as baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: Report human-level performance by comparing individual annotator labels to the majority-vote labels to provide an upper/upper-intermediate bound (authors report human-level performance of 85.5%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use human-level agreement as an interpretable benchmark when assessing model gap to human performance.
